ex.en: She used the apples to make the jam.
ex.zh: 她用蘋果做果醬。

ex.en: This jam jar's lid is stuck and won't open.
ex.zh: 這個果醬罐的蓋子卡住了，打不開。

jam.en: a sweet food made by boiling fruit with sugar

ex.en: We got up at dawn to avoid a traffic jam.
ex.zh: 我們天一亮就起床，以避開塞車。

ex.en: Sorry I'm late; I was stuck in a traffic jam.
ex.zh: 抱歉我遲到了，我塞在車陣裡。

jam.en: a lot of cars in a line that can hardly move

ex.en: The printer jammed again.
ex.zh: 印表機又卡紙了。

ex.en: The paper is jammed in the copier.
ex.zh: 紙卡在影印機裡了。

jam.en: to become stuck and stop working

ex.en: Hundreds of people jammed into the hall.
ex.zh: 數百人擠進大廳。

ex.en: I jammed my clothes into the suitcase.
ex.zh: 我把衣服塞進行李箱。

jam.en: to push many people or things tightly into a space

ex.en: I like to listen to music, especially jazz.
ex.zh: 我喜歡聽音樂，尤其是爵士樂。

ex.en: He likes jazz, and so do I.
ex.zh: 他喜歡爵士樂，我也是。

ex.en: Japanese young people like rock and jazz music.
ex.zh: 日本年輕人喜歡搖滾樂和爵士樂。

jazz.en: a kind of music with strong rhythms where players often make up parts

jazz.zh: jazz up：讓…更有趣、更吸引人

ex.en: Let's jazz up the slides with some photos.
ex.zh: 我們加些照片讓投影片更吸睛吧。

ex.en: She jazzed up the room with colorful pillows.
ex.zh: 她用色彩繽紛的抱枕讓房間更有活力。

jazz.en: to make something more exciting or attractive

ex.en: Put this jacket on, and you'll be much warmer.
ex.zh: 穿上這件外套，你會暖和很多。

ex.en: Do you have this jacket in different colors?
ex.zh: 這件外套有其他顏色嗎？

ex.en: I want the same jacket as you are wearing.
ex.zh: 我想要一件跟你身上穿的一樣的外套。

ex.en: Tom spent more than three years in jail.
ex.zh: 湯姆坐了三年多的牢。

ex.en: How did Tom get out of jail?
ex.zh: 湯姆是怎麼出獄的？

ex.en: How long were you in jail?
ex.zh: 你在監獄裡待了多久？

jail.en: a place where people are kept as punishment or while waiting for trial

ex.en: He was jailed for two years for fraud.
ex.zh: 他因詐欺被判入獄兩年。

ex.en: The driver was jailed for drunk driving.
ex.zh: 那名駕駛因酒駕被關進監獄。

jail.en: to put someone in a place of punishment for a crime

ex.en: The janitor cleans the conference room every evening.
ex.zh: 管理員每天晚上都會清潔會議室。

ex.en: Please tell the janitor about the broken light.
ex.zh: 請告訴管理員那盞燈壞了。

janitor.en: a person whose job is to clean and take care of a building

ex.en: He hit his jaw when he fell off the bike.
ex.zh: 他從腳踏車上摔下來時撞到了下巴。

ex.en: My jaw hurts after the dentist visit.
ex.zh: 看完牙醫後我的下巴很痛。

ex.en: She kept the cookies in a glass jar on the counter.
ex.zh: 她把餅乾放在檯面上的玻璃罐裡。

ex.en: Can you open this jar of jam for me?
ex.zh: 你可以幫我打開這罐果醬嗎？

ex.en: The loud noise jarred me out of my sleep.
ex.zh: 巨大的噪音把我從睡夢中震醒。

ex.en: The sudden crash jarred everyone in the room.
ex.zh: 突然的撞擊聲讓房間裡的每個人都嚇了一跳。

ex.en: James is a common first name in English-speaking countries.
ex.zh: 詹姆斯是英語系國家很常見的名字。

ex.en: James and his cousin built a small boat together.
ex.zh: 詹姆斯和他的表弟一起做了一艘小船。

ex.en: Our new classmate's name is James.
ex.zh: 我們新同學的名字叫詹姆斯。

ex.en: The Lunar New Year often comes in January or February.
ex.zh: 農曆新年常常在一月或二月。

ex.en: It is very cold in January in northern countries.
ex.zh: 北方國家的一月非常冷。

ex.en: The new year begins on the first of January.
ex.zh: 新的一年從一月一日開始。

ex.en: Japan is an island country in East Asia.
ex.zh: 日本是東亞的一個島國。

ex.en: Many tourists visit Japan in spring to see the cherry blossoms.
ex.zh: 許多觀光客在春天造訪日本賞櫻。

ex.en: She studied Japanese in school before moving to Japan.
ex.zh: 她在搬到日本之前就在學校學過日語。

ex.en: Jack is a short and friendly name for John.
ex.zh: 傑克是約翰的一個簡短親切的暱稱。

ex.en: Jack helped his neighbor carry the boxes upstairs.
ex.zh: 傑克幫鄰居把箱子搬上樓。

ex.en: He used a jack to lift the car and change the tire.
ex.zh: 他用千斤頂把車抬起來換輪胎。

ex.en: Make sure the jack is on flat ground before you lift anything.
ex.zh: 抬起東西之前，要確定千斤頂放在平坦的地面上。

ex.en: Plug your headphones into the jack on the side of the laptop.
ex.zh: 把你的耳機插進筆電側邊的插孔。

ex.en: This old phone has a jack for a wired headset.
ex.zh: 這支舊手機有個可接有線耳機的插孔。

ex.en: The Japanese are famous for their polite customs.
ex.zh: 日本人以禮貌的習慣聞名。

ex.en: She has been studying Japanese for two years.
ex.zh: 她已經學了兩年日語。

ex.en: We ate at a small Japanese restaurant near the station.
ex.zh: 我們在車站附近一家小小的日式餐廳用餐。

ex.en: He collects Japanese comic books.
ex.zh: 他收集日本漫畫書。

ex.en: Jane is a simple and classic name for girls.
ex.zh: 簡是一個簡單又經典的女孩名字。

ex.en: Jane enjoys reading novels in the quiet library.
ex.zh: 簡喜歡在安靜的圖書館裡讀小說。

jackson.zh: 傑克遜（美國密西西比州的首府）

ex.en: Jackson is the capital of the state of Mississippi.
ex.zh: 傑克遜是密西西比州的首府。

ex.en: They drove to Jackson to visit a friend over the weekend.
ex.zh: 他們週末開車到傑克遜去探望朋友。

ex.en: A blue jay landed on the fence and screamed.
ex.zh: 一隻藍松鴉停在籬笆上大叫。

ex.en: The jay hid acorns under the leaves for winter.
ex.zh: 松鴉把橡實藏在落葉下準備過冬。

ex.en: Jacob is a common name for boys in many countries.
ex.zh: 雅各在許多國家都是常見的男孩名字。

ex.en: Jacob is one of the people mentioned in the Bible.
ex.zh: 雅各是聖經中提到的人物之一。

ex.en: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean Sea.
ex.zh: 牙買加是加勒比海上的一個島國。

ex.en: Many tourists travel to Jamaica for its beaches.
ex.zh: 許多遊客為了海灘前往牙買加。

ex.en: A jaguar hunts quietly in the rain forest.
ex.zh: 美洲豹在雨林中悄悄地獵食。

ex.en: The jaguar is the largest cat in South America.
ex.zh: 美洲豹是南美洲最大的貓科動物。

ex.en: The doctor explained the result without using medical jargon.
ex.zh: 醫生沒有用醫學術語就解釋了結果。

ex.en: Legal jargon can be hard for ordinary people to follow.
ex.zh: 法律用語對一般人來說可能很難懂。

ex.en: The report was full of technical jargon.
ex.zh: 那份報告充滿了專業術語。

ex.en: The hikers climbed over jagged rocks near the top.
ex.zh: 登山客爬過接近山頂處參差不齊的岩石。

ex.en: He cut his finger on the jagged edge of the can.
ex.zh: 他被罐頭鋸齒狀的邊緣割傷了手指。

ex.en: She wore a bracelet made of green jade.
ex.zh: 她戴著一條綠色玉石做的手鐲。

ex.en: Jade is often seen as a symbol of good luck.
ex.zh: 玉常被視為幸運的象徵。

ex.en: The necklace was made of red jasper stones.
ex.zh: 這條項鍊是用紅色碧玉石做的。

ex.en: Jasper is often used to make small decorative items.
ex.zh: 碧玉常被用來製作小型裝飾品。

ex.en: She jabbed her finger at the map to show me the place.
ex.zh: 她用手指戳著地圖，指給我看那個地方。

ex.en: Don't jab the toast with a sharp knife.
ex.zh: 別用尖刀去戳吐司。

ex.en: He felt a sharp jab in his side.
ex.zh: 他覺得側腰被猛戳了一下。

ex.en: I got my flu jab at the clinic yesterday.
ex.zh: 我昨天在診所打了流感疫苗。

ex.en: Jacqueline is a French girl's name.
ex.zh: 賈桂琳是法文的女子名。

ex.en: Jacqueline works as a nurse in a small clinic.
ex.zh: 賈桂琳在一間小診所擔任護理師。

ex.en: I love Jamaican music, especially reggae.
ex.zh: 我喜歡牙買加音樂，尤其是雷鬼。

ex.en: She cooked a Jamaican dish for dinner.
ex.zh: 她晚餐煮了一道牙買加料理。

ex.en: The Jamaican won the sprint by a wide margin.
ex.zh: 那位牙買加人以明顯的差距贏得短跑。

ex.en: My neighbor is a Jamaican who loves cricket.
ex.zh: 我的鄰居是個愛打板球的牙買加人。

ex.en: I like to drink jasmine tea after dinner.
ex.zh: 我喜歡晚餐後喝茉莉花茶。

ex.en: The garden smelled sweet from the jasmine by the fence.
ex.zh: 籬笆旁的茉莉讓整座花園都散發甜香。

ex.en: After years of the same job, he felt jaded.
ex.zh: 做了多年相同的工作後，他覺得很厭倦。

ex.en: The jaded critic yawned through the whole show.
ex.zh: 那位厭世的評論家整場表演都在打哈欠。

ex.en: Someone in our town won the lottery jackpot.
ex.zh: 我們鎮上有人中了樂透頭獎。

ex.en: The jackpot grows bigger every week nobody wins.
ex.zh: 每週沒人中獎，頭獎獎金就越滾越大。

jackpot.zh: 中大獎；大賺一筆（hit the jackpot）

ex.en: He hit the jackpot when his app became popular.
ex.zh: 他的應用程式爆紅，讓他大賺了一筆。

ex.en: We hit the jackpot with this cheap and great apartment.
ex.zh: 找到這間便宜又棒的公寓，我們真是撿到寶了。

ex.en: Java is the most crowded island in Indonesia.
ex.zh: 爪哇是印尼人口最密集的島嶼。

ex.en: They visited temples on the island of Java.
ex.zh: 他們去了爪哇島上的寺廟參觀。

ex.en: I need a cup of hot java to wake up.
ex.zh: 我需要來杯熱咖啡才能清醒。

ex.en: Let's grab some java before the meeting.
ex.zh: 開會前我們去喝杯咖啡吧。

ex.en: We took a quick jaunt to the coast on Sunday.
ex.zh: 星期天我們到海邊短途旅行了一趟。

ex.en: Their weekend jaunt through the countryside was relaxing.
ex.zh: 他們週末的鄉間小旅行很放鬆。

ex.en: They jaunted around the lake for the afternoon.
ex.zh: 他們整個下午繞著湖邊悠閒遊玩。

ex.en: She likes to jaunt off to the city whenever she is bored.
ex.zh: 她一無聊就愛跑去城裡玩一趟。

ex.en: He wore his hat at a jaunty angle.
ex.zh: 他把帽子戴成一個俏皮的角度。

ex.en: The band played a jaunty tune.
ex.zh: 樂團演奏了一首輕快的曲子。

ex.en: The cafe played a jazzy tune in the background.
ex.zh: 咖啡廳在背景播放著爵士風格的曲子。

ex.en: He gave the old song a jazzy new arrangement.
ex.zh: 他為這首老歌編了一個爵士風的新版本。

ex.en: She wore a jazzy red jacket to the party.
ex.zh: 她穿著一件花俏的紅外套去參加派對。

ex.en: The shop has a jazzy new sign above the door.
ex.zh: 這家店門上有個醒目花俏的新招牌。

ex.en: A jackal howled somewhere in the dark desert.
ex.zh: 黑暗的沙漠某處傳來胡狼的嚎叫。

ex.en: Jackals often hunt in pairs or small groups.
ex.zh: 胡狼常成對或結成小群獵食。

jaundiced.zh: 抱持偏見的；憤世嫉俗的

ex.en: He takes a jaundiced view of every new idea.
ex.zh: 他對每個新點子都抱持偏見的看法。

ex.en: After years of broken promises, she looked at politics with a jaundiced eye.
ex.zh: 多年來承諾落空，她以憤世嫉俗的眼光看待政治。

ex.en: The newborn looked slightly jaundiced and stayed in the hospital.
ex.zh: 那個新生兒看起來有點黃疸，所以留在醫院觀察。

ex.en: A jaundiced skin color can be a sign of liver trouble.
ex.zh: 皮膚發黃可能是肝臟出問題的徵兆。

ex.en: The old jailhouse in town is now a small museum.
ex.zh: 鎮上那座舊監獄現在成了一間小博物館。

ex.en: The sheriff led the man into the jailhouse.
ex.zh: 警長帶那名男子走進了監獄。

ex.en: The jailer unlocked the heavy door each morning.
ex.zh: 獄卒每天早上打開那扇沉重的門。

ex.en: In the old story, the jailer carried the keys on a ring.
ex.zh: 在那個老故事裡，獄卒把鑰匙串在一個環上。

janeiro.zh: 里約熱內盧（Rio de Janeiro）名稱的後半部

ex.en: Rio de Janeiro is a famous city in Brazil.
ex.zh: 里約熱內盧是巴西的一座著名城市。

ex.en: The name Janeiro is the Portuguese word for January.
ex.zh: Janeiro 這個字在葡萄牙語中是一月的意思。

ex.en: The keys jangled in his pocket as he walked.
ex.zh: 他走路時，口袋裡的鑰匙叮噹作響。

ex.en: Her bracelets jangle every time she waves.
ex.zh: 她每次揮手，手鐲都會叮噹作響。

ex.en: I woke up to the jangle of the alarm bell.
ex.zh: 我被刺耳的鈴聲吵醒。

ex.en: The jangle of coins filled the empty room.
ex.zh: 硬幣的叮噹聲充滿了空蕩的房間。
